Kenji López-Alt Sep 8, 2026 View in app View in app Hi everyone, I wanted to take a quick moment to correct something I said in my latest knife-sharpening video . In that video, I repeated a very common explanation of the difference between sharpening and honing: Sharpening on a whetstone removes metal, while honing on a honing rod merely realigns a rolled edge back into its original shape. This is the explanation I was taught everywhere from other restaurant cooks and chefs, to my fellow editors and test cooks at Cook’s Illustrated and Serious Eats. It’s one of those things I’ve repeated so many times that I’ve never really considered that it may be incorrect. So when a number of folks in the comments pointed out that research exists proving that honing does, in fact, remove metal from the blade, I went back and did some reading, particularly from an excellent website called Science of Sharp . The author has done a huge number of experiments using a scanning electron microscope to look at blade edges before and after sharpening, stropping, honing, and actual use.
